answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can hold each agent's earnings in escrow that releases slowly, like a trellis guiding a vine rather than letting it sprawl overnight. New identities start on an isolated island of low trust with tiny limits, and only a steady pulse of useful, verified work over time unlocks larger payouts, while random audits claw back escrow from fakes. Creating thousands of copies therefore costs time without accelerating rewards.
